Proposition
[divergence as a trace of $L_Xg$]

Source: petersen:page-0067 ↗ def:pet-ch2-divergence-lie-derivative

For a positively oriented orthonormal frame $E_1,\dots ,E_n$, $\operatorname {div}X=\sum _i rac12(L_Xg)(E_i,E_i)$; consequently $\Delta f=\operatorname {div} abla f=\sum _i\operatorname {Hess}f(E_i,E_i)$.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch2-divergence-trace-formula

\sketch Choose an oriented orthonormal frame $E_1,\dots ,E_n$. Since $\mathrm{vol}(E_1,\dots ,E_n)=1$,

\[ \operatorname {div}X =(L_X\mathrm{vol})(E_1,\dots ,E_n) =-\sum _i g(L_XE_i,E_i). \]

Because $g(E_i,E_i)=1$, $(L_Xg)(E_i,E_i)=-2g(L_XE_i,E_i)$. Summation gives the divergence formula; applying it to $X= abla f$ gives the Laplacian formula.

□
